skill.name: remembering-conversations
skill.description: Search past Claude Code conversations through episodic memory to recover decisions, patterns, fixes, and context before solving similar problems.
skill.summary: Recall prior conversation context before making implementation decisions.
skill.author: obra

security_audit.summary: The shell execution and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting and normal workflow prose. The documented read API can access archived conversation JSONL files under a hidden configuration directory, so the filesystem and privacy risk is real. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning and require scoped user intent before reading full historical conversations.
Use placeholder paths and state that agents should only read files returned by the memory search tool.
Prefer snippets, source references, and limited line ranges before loading entire conversation archives.

semantic_findings.title: Conversation History Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to search past conversations and read top results, then synthesize findings with sources. This can reveal sensitive information from archived chats if searches are too broad or unapproved.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly uses a search agent to read past conversation results, and the MCP reference defines a read tool for full conversation content. This is intended functionality, so the risk is privacy exposure rather than covert exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Past decisions and fixes can be hard to find during active work. This skill searches conversation history so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can reuse prior context.
actual_capabilities: Dispatches a search-conversations subagent for historical lookup tasks.
Searches episodic memory for prior decisions, patterns, fixes, and context.
Reads selected top results and synthesizes actionable findings with sources.
Supports semantic, text, and combined search modes through the MCP reference.
Guides when to search memory and when to inspect the current codebase first.
Discourages direct MCP tool use to reduce context usage.
limitations: Requires the episodic-memory plugin and an existing conversation archive.
May expose sensitive prior conversation content if searches are too broad.
Does not replace current codebase inspection or current conversation context.
Search quality depends on archived conversations and available indexes.

use_cases.title: Recover Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Find earlier reasoning about a project choice before changing related code.

use_cases.title: Resume Prior Work
use_cases.description: Locate previous implementation notes, blockers, and next steps for an interrupted task.

use_cases.title: Avoid Repeated Debugging
use_cases.description: Search for similar past failures and reuse confirmed fixes when the current issue matches.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Past Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one known topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search past conversations for why we chose [approach] in [project]. Summarize the decision, tradeoffs, and sources.

prompt_templates.title: Reuse a Debugging Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate lookup for a recurring failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search memory for prior work on [error or symptom]. Focus on confirmed fixes, failed attempts, and relevant source references.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Prior Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning across multiple related topics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search past conversations for [pattern A] and [pattern B]. Compare where each worked, where each failed, and what applies now.

prompt_templates.title: Plan With Historical Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning after current code exploration.
prompt_templates.prompt: After inspecting the current code, search memory for related architecture discussions. Produce a plan that separates historical facts from current assumptions.

output_examples.input: How should we handle auth redirects? We discussed this before.
output_examples.output: The skill searches memory for the prior auth redirect discussion, then returns the earlier decision, tradeoffs, and source conversations.

output_examples.input: I am stuck on the release workflow. Check whether we solved this before.
output_examples.output: The skill looks for matching release workflow conversations and summarizes previous blockers, successful steps, and remaining cautions.

output_examples.input: Before changing the caching layer, find our past reasoning about it.
output_examples.output: The skill retrieves relevant caching discussions and separates confirmed historical decisions from items that need current verification.

best_practices: Search after you understand the current task and likely topic.
Use focused queries with project names, feature names, symptoms, or decisions.
Verify historical conclusions against the current code before acting.
anti_patterns: Searching memory before understanding what the user needs.
Loading entire conversations when snippets and limited ranges are enough.
Treating memory results as current truth without checking the repository.

faq.question: What does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches archived Claude Code conversations through the episodic-memory MCP tools.

faq.question: Does it search the current repository?
faq.answer: No. Use normal code inspection tools for the current repository before relying on memory.

faq.question: Can it read full conversations?
faq.answer: Yes. The referenced MCP tool can read conversation files, including selected line ranges.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after understanding the task, when prior decisions or repeated problems may matter.

faq.question: What privacy risk exists?
faq.answer: Search results and full reads can expose sensitive content from previous conversations.

faq.question: How should results be used?
faq.answer: Use results as historical context, then verify them against current files and requirements.
